quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to that vehicle.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all your vehicle's windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors.

questions.question: When you drive through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Pass carefully and do not look at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not look at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things in construction zones. This causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: If you are 21 years old or older and your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is ____ or higher, you are breaking the law.

options.text: 0.08 percent
0.06 percent
0.04 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means your license will be suspended for 30 days and you may face criminal penalties. Repeat offenses lead to harsher punishments.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Slow down to prevent it.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: In rain, drive slower to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast makes your tires lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles using sirens and lights. Drive to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the other vehicle.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly to get back to your lane faster. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, check for vehicles to your side and behind you. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions just ahead. This sign tells you to be ready for traffic merging from the right.

questions.question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal turns, lane changes, and slowdowns in advance. This helps the driver behind you maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you know?

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt less well than concrete or asphalt. On gravel or dirt roads, slow down. Stopping takes longer and skidding is easier when turning.

questions.question: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm is extended, you must stay stopped. Continue waiting until the lights turn off, the stop arm goes in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: Which of these factors causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Driving faster than the speed limit or driving too fast for the road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Looking around and paying attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving faster than the speed limit or driving too fast for the road conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at legal speeds and match the flow of traffic around you.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Making sudden, unsafe lane changes.
How many passengers are in the car.
Driving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sudden, unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while driving. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not react to them. The safest thing to do is stay away from them.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: To turn, use the lane that is closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, look for cars, and enter when it is safe.
Look for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering traffic.
Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering a highway. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic already on the highway, then smoothly merge in.

questions.question: The traditional mirror setting:

options.text: Works well for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight spaces.
Does not show the edge of the vehicle.
Works for all vehicles in all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works well for large vehicles when towing or backing in tight spaces.
questions.explanation: After adjusting your seat, set your left mirror to see the left edge of your vehicle and your right mirror to see the right edge. This traditional setting works best for trucks, vans, and SUVs when towing or backing in tight spaces.
